headline: Stocks Look to Steady After Monday's Broad Rout, With Chips and Gulf Tensions in Focus
body_html:
Wall Street heads into Tuesday trying to recover from a lopsided Monday, November 16. Of the 664 stocks we track, 504 fell and only 157 rose. Financials dropped 5.83% and semiconductors lost 5.2%, the two worst sectors. Reports pointed to tech weakness as investors positioned ahead of a closely watched chipmaker earnings report.

Geopolitics remains the other backdrop. Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have increased, and Washington has condemned Iranian strikes in Bahrain. Even so, oil slipped as recovering Middle East exports eased supply worries. Energy shares fell 3.22% on the day, so the open will show whether that weakness carries over or crude steadies. Materials lost 2.21% and industrials 1.42%.

At the open, watch whether chip and financial names stabilize after the heavy selling. Software was the most resilient group at just 0.44% lower, led by HubSpot, up 6.78%. Bullish, down 12.18%, was the biggest decliner. Early moves are thin and unreliable, so the first hour matters more than the first print. The next session after today is Wednesday, November 18.

briefs.headline: Oman and Iran Discuss Keeping Sea Lanes Open
briefs.body: Officials from Oman and Iran talked about safeguarding maritime corridors as attacks around the Strait of Hormuz picked up. The diplomacy is an attempt to contain risks to shipping. Traders will watch whether talks calm the region or incidents keep escalating.

briefs.headline: Crude Eases as Middle East Supply Recovers
briefs.body: Oil slipped as recovering exports from the Middle East offset worries over Gulf tensions. Energy stocks still fell 3.22% on Monday, the third-worst sector move in our universe. The open will test whether crude holds its softer tone.

briefs.headline: Japan Floats Regional Oil Security Task Force
briefs.body: Japan proposed an Asia-wide task force on oil security at the ASEAN summit. The idea reflects concern among energy importers about disruptions in the Gulf. No details on membership or timing were given, so it is an early signal rather than a policy shift.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Slump Before a Key Earnings Report
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 5.2% on Monday as tech weakness spread ahead of a major chipmaker's results. Tower Semiconductor lost 9.17% and Applied Optoelectronics 9.48%. Investors will look for any sign of stabilization at the open.

briefs.headline: United Airlines Clears Technology Outage
briefs.body: United Airlines said a system problem that delayed departing flights has been resolved. The outage disrupted morning schedules before the fix. Travelers may still see knock-on delays as the carrier restores normal operations.

briefs.headline: Software Holds Up Better Than the Rest
briefs.body: Software was the best-performing sector on a weak Monday, down 0.44%. HubSpot rose 6.78%, Qualys 5.24% and Freshworks 4.42%. The group's resilience stood out against steep losses in financials and chips.
